tips.title: The command palette runs everything
tips.body: Every action in Thor is in the palette, with the chord it is bound to beside it. It is the fastest way to find a command whose name you only half remember.

tips.title: Open a file by its name
tips.body: Quick open searches the whole workspace by file name. Type a few letters of the path to narrow it further.

tips.title: Edit with more than one caret
tips.body: Ctrl and a click puts another caret in the buffer, and the chord below adds one on the line under the last. Every caret then types, moves and deletes together.

tips.title: Select the next occurrence
tips.body: The first press selects the word under the caret, each one after that the next occurrence of it, with a caret of its own. Rename a local variable without leaving the keyboard.

tips.title: Two files side by side
tips.body: The editor splits into two panes. Each pane keeps its own tab, so a header and its implementation stay on screen together.

tips.title: Name your build commands
tips.body: Put the commands you run often in .thor/tasks.json. Each one gets a name in the title bar selector, and the chord below runs the selected one in the console.

tips.title: One shell per console tab
tips.body: The + in the console opens another terminal, from every shell found on the machine. Each shell stays alive between commands, so cd and environment variables persist.

tips.title: Go to the definition
tips.body: Jumps to where the symbol under the caret is declared; ctrl and a click does the same. Thor analyzes Odin in the editor itself, and uses a language server for the other languages.

tips.title: Go back where you came from
tips.body: The jump list remembers each place you jumped from, so a walk through several definitions retraces in the order you made it.

tips.title: Find every use of a symbol
tips.body: Lists everywhere the symbol under the caret is used. Rename Symbol in the palette then changes all of them at once, instead of one search and replace at a time.

tips.title: Let the editor fix it
tips.body: Offers the code actions for the caret: the import a name needs, the unused declaration to drop, the fix for the error under it.

tips.title: Format the file you are in
tips.body: The Odin formatter is built in, so no external tool is needed. Turn on format_on_save in the settings to run it before every explicit save.

tips.title: Read Markdown as a page
tips.body: Renders the Markdown file in the pane instead of showing its source. The manual under Help opens the same way.

tips.title: Fold what you are not reading
tips.body: Folds the block at the caret; the arrow beside a line number does the same with the mouse. A folded block stays folded while you work elsewhere in the file.

tips.title: Find the symbol, not the file
tips.body: Searches every symbol in the workspace by name. Go to Symbol does the same inside the file you are in.

tips.title: Comment out a block
tips.body: Comments the selected lines with the marker of their language, and uncomments them when they already carry it.

tips.title: Move a line without cutting it
tips.body: Carries the line, or the whole selection, past its neighbour. The duplicate chords leave a copy behind instead.

tips.title: Every folder keeps its own session
tips.body: Thor remembers the open tabs and the panel layout per folder. Reopen the folder and you are back where you left it.

tips.title: Settings per workspace
tips.body: A .thor/ folder in the workspace overlays your own settings, keybindings, tasks and language servers. Only the keys it names change, so the rest still comes from your defaults.

tips.title: Languages are plugins
tips.body: Each language is a small Lua plugin under plugins/. A workspace can carry its own in .thor/plugins, and Thor asks before it loads one.
